metadata.title: Lipofection: Transient Transfection of Mammalian Cells with Lipofectamine 3000 (24-well)
metadata.purpose: Introduce plasmid DNA into adherent mammalian cells by complexing the DNA with the cationic lipid Lipofectamine 3000 (plus P3000 enhancer) in Opti-MEM and applying the DNA-lipid complexes to cells for transient gene expression.
metadata.scope: Lipid-mediated transient transfection of adherent mammalian cells in a 24-well plate using Lipofectamine 3000 with plasmid DNA. Amounts are the manufacturer's 24-well values (two-dose optimization). For siRNA, omit P3000 Reagent. Stable transfection and electroporation are out of scope.
metadata.estimatedTime: Day 0 seed cells; Day 1 transfect (10 min prep + 10-15 min complex formation); Day 2-4 analyze
beforeYouBegin: Seed cells so they are 70-90% confluent at the time of transfection.
Prepare complexes in serum-free Opti-MEM; it is not necessary to remove complexes or change medium after transfection.
Test two doses of Lipofectamine 3000 (0.75 and 1.5 uL for 24-well) to find the optimum for your cells.

materials.name: Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent
materials.rawText: Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent per well: 0.75 and 1.5 uL (24-well)

materials.name: P3000 Reagent
materials.specification: DNA enhancer supplied with Lipofectamine 3000; omit for siRNA

materials.name: Plasmid DNA
materials.specification: Purified plasmid; 1 ug used per 24-well reaction (delivers ~500 ng per well)

materials.name: Opti-MEM I Reduced Serum Medium
materials.specification: Serum-free medium for diluting reagent and DNA
materials.rawText: Dilute Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent in Opti-MEM Medium; dilute DNA in Opti-MEM Medium

materials.name: Complete growth medium
materials.specification: Normal culture medium on the cells; complexes may be added in presence or absence of serum/antibiotic
materials.rawText: Make DNA-Lipofectamine 3000 complexes ... in the presence or absence of serum/antibiotic

samples.name: Adherent mammalian cells (70-90% confluent)
samples.description: Cells seeded one day earlier to reach 70-90% confluency at transfection.

samples.name: DNA-lipid complex
samples.description: Plasmid DNA + P3000 combined 1:1 with diluted Lipofectamine 3000 in Opti-MEM.

samples.name: Transfected cells
samples.description: Cells that have taken up the DNA-lipid complex and transiently express the delivered gene.

tables.title: Lipofectamine 3000 reaction components (24-well, two-dose optimization)
rows: Diluted DNA added to each lipid tube (1:1)
tables.note: Each reaction mix is for one well and accounts for pipetting variation; scale proportionally for more wells. Delivers ~500 ng DNA and 1 uL P3000 per well.

steps.action: Seed cells so they will be 70-90% confluent at the time of transfection.

parameters.rawText: Seed cells to be 70-90% confluent at transfection

steps.action: Dilute Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent in Opti-MEM in two tubes (one per dose) and mix well by vortexing 2-3 sec.
steps.criticalNotes: Prepare two Lipofectamine 3000 doses to determine the optimum amount for your cells.

steps.action: Prepare a master mix of DNA by diluting DNA in Opti-MEM, then add P3000 Reagent and mix well.

branches.condition: if transfecting siRNA instead of plasmid DNA
branches.action: Do NOT add P3000 Reagent when diluting the nucleic acid (step 3).

steps.action: Add the diluted DNA to each tube of diluted Lipofectamine 3000 at a 1:1 ratio and mix.

parameters.rawText: Diluted DNA (with P3000): 25 uL; Diluted Lipofectamine 3000: 25 uL (24-well)
Add Diluted DNA to each tube of Diluted Lipofectamine 3000 Reagent (1:1 ratio)

steps.action: Incubate the DNA-lipid mixture at room temperature to allow complexes to form.

parameters.rawText: Incubate for 10-15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.action: Add the DNA-lipid complex to the cells (one complex volume per well).
steps.criticalNotes: It is not necessary to remove complexes or change/add medium after transfection.

steps.action: Incubate the cells at 37 C, then visualize/analyze the transfected cells.

parameters.rawText: Incubate cells for 2-4 days at 37 C.

steps.expectedResult: Transient expression of the delivered gene; optimal Lipofectamine 3000 dose identified by comparing the two doses.

controls.name: Untransfected (mock) cells
controls.description: Cells receiving reagent complexes made without DNA, or no treatment; baseline for expression and reagent toxicity.

controls.name: Positive-control reporter plasmid
controls.description: A well-expressing reporter (e.g. GFP) to confirm transfection efficiency.

expectedOutputs: Cells transiently expressing the delivered gene, assayable 24-72 h (2-4 days) post-transfection.
Optimal Lipofectamine 3000 dose for the cell line, from the two-dose comparison.

troubleshooting.cause: Suboptimal lipid dose, low confluency, or poor DNA quality
troubleshooting.solution: Test both lipid doses, transfect at 70-90% confluency, use clean plasmid prep

troubleshooting.cause: Too much lipid or too long an exposure for sensitive cells
troubleshooting.solution: Use the lower (0.75 uL) dose; optionally change medium a few hours post-transfection

troubleshooting.cause: P3000 omitted for DNA, or complexes not formed
troubleshooting.solution: Include P3000 for plasmid DNA (omit only for siRNA); allow 10-15 min complex formation

safety: Follow aseptic cell-culture practice; handle recombinant DNA per institutional biosafety rules.
Opti-MEM and transfection reagents are for research use only; wear gloves.
Biosafety level depends on the cell line and the encoded insert.
limitations: Provides transient (not stable) expression; efficiency and toxicity are cell-line dependent and require dose optimization. Amounts shown are the manufacturer's 24-well values; the source does not fix the cell line or the specific plasmid.
